question:
Someone who has never been where you live will picture something very different from what you know. Describe your world so clearly that they get it right.

Steps:
1. Start recording. Pick one topic from the list below.
2. Say a short, vague version in 5 words or fewer.
3. Now say a detailed version. You can use your own experience or make one up, but don’t say real names, addresses, or the name of your school. Include at least 3 details, such as what people are doing, what it looks like, and what you hear or smell.
4. Tell the camera one thing a listener could get wrong if they only heard the short version.

Topic list:
- A celebration
- A family meal
- A game kids play outside
- A morning at home

rubric.description: Student does not say a description on camera.

Student attempts the task but does not meet Level 2. For example, the student says only a short version or only a detailed version, the short version is longer than 5 words, or the detailed version has fewer than 3 details.
Student says a short version (5 words or fewer) AND a detailed version with at least 3 details.
Meets all of the above AND names a specific thing a listener could get wrong if they only heard the short version (for example, “they might picture a cake, but we eat rice”).
